CLL/SLL is top-ranked due to high prevalence of constitutional symptoms, lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly (causing abdominal fullness), and weight loss; CD5+/CD23+ co-expression would be confirmatory (though not yet tested). Hodgkin lymphoma ranks second given classic B-symptoms, cervical adenopathy, and systemic inflammation—though abdominal involvement is less common without mediastinal or para-aortic nodes. DLBCL is highly plausible given aggressive tempo, B-symptoms, and nodal/extranodal presentation (e.g., GI tract or peritoneum causing fullness). Mantle cell lymphoma fits the age-adjusted presentation (often >60 years), B-symptoms, lymphadenopathy, and gastrointestinal involvement (e.g., 'lymphomatous polyposis' causing fullness), though CD5+/CD23− immunophenotype makes it less likely than CLL/SLL pending flow. ALPS is included as a rare non-malignant cause of chronic lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and cytopenias—but lacks typical B-symptoms like drenching night sweats or rapid weight loss, and rarely presents de novo in adulthood with this acuity; hence low confidence."}
